similarity_meaning_lunar_base.text: Each Earth point is paired with its lunar twin: the 1-degree cell, among NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole, that holds the same thermal position and has a similar terrain. The coldest temperature and the daily temperature swing are compared as positions: where the point ranks among Earth's lunar-base candidates against where its twin ranks among the cells of the nine regions, each within 10 percentile points; the two places are not equally cold and the real values are far apart. Slope and roughness are compared in real values (the twin within 4 degrees and 60 m). The real values on both sides and their differences are shown next to every pair.
similarity_meaning_lunar_base.where: lunar_base (percentile_and_real_tolerance rule): wherever a similarity is shown, next to each variable's percentile on both sides (earth_lunar_base_pairs.bin '<variable>.earth_pct', '.moon_pct', '.diff_pct') and the real values and differences ('<variable>.earth', '.moon', '.diff', 'info.<variable>.*')

lunar_base_pair_sentence.text: This pair matches by relative thermal position, not by equal temperatures: this site's coldest temperature and daily swing rank among Earth's lunar-base candidates where its twin's rank among the cells of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole. In real values the twin is {temp_diff_k} K colder on average (minimum {tmin_moon_c} °C at the surface against {tmin_earth_c} °C air temperature here) and its day-night swing is {amp_diff_k} K larger; slope differs by {slope_diff}° and roughness by {rough_diff} m.

temp_diff_k.meaning: mean temperature, Earth minus twin, in K (the twin is colder on every pair: checked by a test)

tmin_moon_c.meaning: the twin's coldest SURFACE temperature (Diviner, measured), K converted to degrees C

tmin_earth_c.meaning: the Earth point's coldest AIR temperature (WorldClim, modelled), K converted to degrees C

amp_diff_k.meaning: daily temperature swing, twin minus Earth, in K (the twin's is larger on every pair: checked by a test)

variants.no_cell_meets_either: No lunar twin: no cell of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole matches this point's thermal position (closest: {variable} {gap} points away) or its terrain (closest: {variable2} {gap2} {unit2} away). lunar_base_swing_gate.text: The Lunar base keeps the team's gate 'daily thermal swing at least 15 K'. Without it, Earth cells with a swing of about 1 K (for example on Ellesmere Island) would match the Moon's coldest temperature at a similarity of about 99, and the key variable, the thermal swing, would carry no weight in practice. The recognised polar stations therefore do not pass: daily land-surface swing Haughton crater (Devon Island, cell E5130) 2.5 K; Svalbard, Bockfjorden (cell E3793) 1.2 K; Kangerlussuaq, ice-sheet margin (cell E8049) 6.6 K; McMurdo and Concordia have no land-surface temperature in the table. They are analogs of cold and isolation, not of thermal cycling.

known_limitations: lunar_base is an exact copy of the team's thermal block (team design values, no external source). The ice block is shown per Earth cell as information only (passes or not, its suitability) and never changes this ranking; no lunar cell passes ice because lunar permafrost_class is the MODELLED label 'ninguno', which the ice gate excludes.

Similarity is a likeness of thermal POSITION and real terrain, not of temperature (team decision of 2026-11-15 08:55 CET; missions.json similarity, rule percentile_and_real_tolerance): the coldest temperature and the daily temperature swing are compared as percentiles within each population (Earth: the points passing this mission's funnel; Moon: the cells of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole), each within 10 percentile points, and slope and roughness in real values (within 4 deg and 60 m). Equal positions do not mean equal temperatures: on every pair the twin is far colder and swings far more than the Earth point, and the real values and differences are shown with every pair (similarity.json texts.lunar_base_pair_sentence). A point with no such cell keeps its suitability but has no twin, no similarity and no final score (missions.json similarity.unpaired_by_kind).

The coldest temperature (tmin_c) is a MODELLED air temperature on Earth (WorldClim, coldest month, interpolated) and a MEASURED surface temperature on the Moon (Diviner night minimum); the Earth diurnal amplitude is a difference between two satellite overpasses and understates the daily range. Both are suitability criteria on Earth, and in the similarity only their position within each population is compared, never their values.
Antarctica has no land surface temperature product here, so its cells fail on lst_diurnal_amp_k with 'no data' (missing_data).
The list is ordered by the final score: 50 % similarity to the lunar twin and 50 % suitability for the mission. These are five of the highest-scoring analogs in our model, not a proven best.
Stability figures pending the independent re-audit.

The Lunar base keeps the team's gate 'daily thermal swing at least 15 K'. Without it, Earth cells with a swing of about 1 K (for example on Ellesmere Island) would match the Moon's coldest temperature at a similarity of about 99, and the key variable, the thermal swing, would carry no weight in practice. The recognised polar stations therefore do not pass: daily land-surface swing Haughton crater (Devon Island, cell E5130) 2.5 K; Svalbard, Bockfjorden (cell E3793) 1.2 K; Kangerlussuaq, ice-sheet margin (cell E8049) 6.6 K; McMurdo and Concordia have no land-surface temperature in the table. They are analogs of cold and isolation, not of thermal cycling.

The Lunar base suitability uses one criterion for the ground instead of two: the bare-or-sparse fraction (from ESA CCI land cover, continuous, without the urban class) weighs 25 %; the thermal-inertia class (built from the same land-cover classes) and the permafrost class (modelled, missing on 607 of 2,419 passing points, with no sourced link to a base) carry no weight. The thermal-inertia class is still required and still excludes water.
